title_en: Fallout 3 — F3DAD Orphan MGEF/SCPT/ACTI/CONT Reference-Graph Audit v1.1

analysis_receipts.note: These hashes identify locally generated analysis outputs/scripts, not Bethesda primary assets.

targets: revision families and structurally adjacent implementations

evidence_levels.P0: Record/subrecord/script bytes exist in a shipped official master from the registered archive.
evidence_levels.P1: A reference/placement relation is directly reconstructed from FormID-bearing records.
evidence_levels.P2: Script source retained in the master establishes intended control flow.
evidence_levels.P3: Test-cell-only, unplaced or orphan status is established within the inspected static graph.
evidence_levels.P4: Public-footprint checks distinguish already documented cut content from graph details worth preserving.
evidence_levels.P5: Runtime reachability remains a separate gate whenever enable-parent, quest result scripts or engine semantics can alter static conclusions.

methodology.false_positive_policy: A static absence of direct Enable text or direct placement is not sufficient to label an object impossible to reach at runtime.

activation_chain: stage 200 counts supported alien weapons inside the container
stage 200 re-adds the same weapon forms

quest_stage_200.label: ALIEN WEAPON REPAIR CONTAINER FUNCTION
script_blocks_observed: Count Weapons in Container - set variables
quest_stage_200.mechanism_interpretation: The remove-and-re-add pipeline is explicitly organized as a repair-container function. Static ESM evidence establishes the intended repair pipeline; exact runtime condition restoration is not claimed as independently runtime-tested in this audit.

relationship_to_stage_100_recharge_stati.stage_100_label: OBSOLETE ---- ALIEN WEAPON REPAIR STATION FUNCTION
relationship_to_stage_100_recharge_stati.stage_100_behavior: Counts supported alien weapons in player inventory, removes them, re-adds them, restores the previously equipped supported weapon and resets variables.
relationship_to_stage_100_recharge_stati.placement_observation: One placement observed, and it is inside developer test cell DLC05TestPhil.
relationship_to_stage_100_recharge_stati.key_distinction: Stage 100 is the test-cell recharge-station path; stage 200 is a separate container-mediated design whose base container has no observed placement in shipped Zeta.esm.

public_footprint.admitted_claim: The shipped ESM independently reconstructs a distinct unplaced stage-200 repair-container implementation in addition to the publicly documented test-cell recharge station.

findings.graph: WEAP -> PROJ -> EXPL -> Vol1 ACTI/SCPT -> recursively spawned Vol2 ACTI/SCPT

script_semantics.vol1: Marks the first triggering actor with detectLifeRange=1, spawns Vol2 and TrapGasFire01, then later clears the first actor marker.
script_semantics.vol2: Only propagates when triggerActor.detectLifeRange == 0; marks that actor, spawns another Vol2 and TrapGasFire01, then self-disables after a timeout.
script_semantics.interpretation: detectLifeRange is repurposed as a transient visited-target flag for recursive chain propagation.

findings.research_value: Preserves the exact visited-target implementation primitive rather than re-claiming discovery of the weapon.

script_behavior: On ScriptEffectStart, if gore is enabled, applies Smoke01.
If target is dead at start, also applies pulseDisableFXShader.
On ScriptEffectFinish, removes both visual shaders.

weapon_a_correction.display_name: Electric Sword A Electrocute Crit Knockdown
weapon_a_correction.meaning: The surviving orphan MGEF is not statically connected as the normal enchantment of testPhilElectricSwordA.

intended_behavior_if_uncommented: At <=30% health it would remove DLC05AlienShieldSpell and stop future shield flashes.
Otherwise a 0.6-second timer would clear the hit-flash shader.

findings.claim: This is dead/incomplete prototype code, not a functional hidden shield obtainable in the released runtime.

states_observed.-1: standing on pad / light shader state

findings.interpretation: The test script and explicitly obsolete door scripts preserve an earlier actor-state teleport orchestration family; this is architecture/revision evidence rather than a hidden player item.
An earlier ferris-wheel encounter controller survives alongside the later main script, including a different final-wave timing threshold.

records.behavior: Reports START/END via showwarning and accumulates elapsed seconds into actor variable01.
Restores left/right mobility, left/right attack, perception and endurance limb-condition actor values by 100.

findings.research_role: Negative/control examples showing that a high orphan score can represent a generic developer utility rather than meaningful hidden game content.

counterexample.meaning: A naive disabled-ref/no-direct-Enable filter captures a known game object, proving the rule is insufficient.

new_gate: Resolve quest-stage result scripts that Enable/Disable references.
Only then classify a disabled reference as STATICALLY_UNREACHABLE_CANDIDATE.

public_footprint_controls.note: The test cell and the 100%-repair recharge-station mechanic are already described publicly; v1.1 does not claim discovery of them.

The public container index lists xx0066F4 / DLC05WeapRepairContainer, but the indexed checks performed for this audit did not surface a dedicated explanation of its stage-200 RepairContainerRef pipeline.
Public documentation already associates it with chain-reaction/Tesla-cannon debugging.
Excluded from novelty; retained as a public-footprint control.

most_important_result.statement: The strongest new structural result of v1.1 is the distinct unplaced DLC05WeapRepairContainer -> RepairContainerRef -> DLC05AlienTechFunctions stage 200 pipeline, separate from the already documented DLC05TestPhil recharge-station implementation.

next_gate.purpose: Resolve the 451 initially-disabled references through XESP enable-parent, quest-stage, controller and linked-reference semantics before promoting any world-ghost object to unreachable/secret status.
